questions.question: If Girl A takes 20 s and Girl B takes 50 s to climb a rope, both performing 3200 J of work, their difference in performance is characterised by which physical concept?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the **rate of doing work** or the rate at which energy is transferred or transformed. In this scenario, while both girls perform the same amount of work, the time taken differs, which directly affects the power output.
 
• The formula for Power is **Power (P) = Work (W) / Time (t)**. This indicates that power is inversely proportional to time when the work done is constant.
 
• For **Girl A**, the work done is **3200 J** and the time taken is **20 s**. Her power output is calculated as 3200 / 20 = **160 Watts**.
 
• For **Girl B**, the work done is **3200 J** and the time taken is **50 s**. Her power output is calculated as 3200 / 50 = **64 Watts**.
 
• Since the **total work done (3200 J)** is identical for both, the difference in their performance—where Girl A completes the task faster than Girl B—is specifically characterized by their **Power**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Power.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SI Unit of Power:** The standard unit of power is the **Watt (W)**, which is equivalent to **one Joule per second (1 J/s)**. It is named after the Scottish inventor **James Watt**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Power is a **scalar quantity** because it only has magnitude and no specific direction. It depends only on the magnitude of work and the time interval.
 
• **Work and Energy:** **Work** is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force. In this question, both girls consumed **3200 J** of energy to perform the task, but the "speed" of that energy consumption is what defines power.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** This is the force of attraction between two masses. While the girls are working against gravity to climb the rope, the **gravitational force** acting on them depends on their **mass** and the **acceleration due to gravity (9.8 m/s²)**, not the time taken.
 
• **Total Displacement:** This refers to the change in position. Since both are climbing the same rope to the same height, their **total displacement** is equal and does not explain the difference in performance over time.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for power is **[M¹ L² T⁻³]**. This is derived from the dimensions of work [M¹ L² T⁻²] divided by time [T].
 
• **Commercial Unit:** While Watt is the SI unit, **Horsepower (hp)** is often used in the automotive and engineering industries. **1 hp** is approximately equal to **746 Watts**.

questions.question: For a distinct echo to be heard, the minimum time interval between the original sound and the reflected sound should be approximately ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1 s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **echo** is the phenomenon where a sound is heard again after it is **reflected** back from a hard surface like a wall, mountain, or cliff.
 
• To hear a distinct echo, the sensation of the original sound must have faded from the human brain. The **persistence of hearing** for a human ear is approximately **0.1 seconds**.
 
• This means that the **time interval** between the original sound and the reflected sound must be at least **0.1 s** for the human brain to distinguish them as two separate sounds.
 
• If the reflected sound arrives in less than **0.1 s**, the two sounds merge, and we hear a prolonged sound rather than a distinct echo.
 
• The total distance covered by the sound (from the source to the obstacle and back) must be such that the time taken is **0.1 s** or more. At a standard speed of sound in air (approx. **344 m/s** at **22°C**), this total distance is **34.4 meters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calculation of Minimum Distance:**

 
 
• The minimum distance required to hear an echo can be calculated using the formula: **Distance = (Speed × Time) / 2**.
 
• Using the standard speed of **344 m/s** and the minimum time of **0.1 s**, the distance is (**344 × 0.1) / 2 = 17.2 meters**.
 
• Therefore, to hear a clear echo, the obstacle must be at least **17.2 meters** away from the source of the sound.
 
 
 
• **Reverberation:**
 
 
• When sound is reflected multiple times in a closed space (like a large hall), the reflections persist and blur the original sound; this is known as **reverberation**.
 
• Unlike an echo, which is a single distinct reflection, **reverberation** is the persistence of sound due to repeated reflections arriving in less than **0.1 s**.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Speed of Sound:**
 
 
• The speed of sound varies with the **temperature** of the medium. For every **1 degree Celsius** rise in temperature, the speed of sound increases by approximately **0.6 m/s**.
 
• As the speed of sound increases with temperature, the **minimum distance** required to hear an echo also increases on a hot day.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nature of Surfaces:** Echoes are best heard when the reflecting surface is **large, hard, and distant**. Soft surfaces like curtains or carpets absorb sound and prevent echoes.
 
• **Applications of Reflection:** The principle of sound reflection and echo is used in **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) to measure the depth of the sea and in **Ultrasound** imaging for medical diagnostics.
 
• **Speed in Media:** Sound travels fastest in **solids**, followed by **liquids**, and slowest in **gases**. In water, the speed of sound is roughly **1500 m/s**, which would significantly increase the minimum distance needed for an echo compared to air.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic reaction of saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Substitution reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons**, also known as **alkanes**, are organic compounds consisting entirely of **single covalent bonds** between carbon atoms. Their general chemical formula is **CnH2n+2**.
 
• Because all the valencies of carbon atoms are fully satisfied by single bonds, alkanes are relatively **unreactive** under normal conditions. They do not have double or triple bonds to "open up" for new atoms.
 
• The characteristic reaction of alkanes is the **Substitution reaction**. In this process, one or more **hydrogen atoms** of the hydrocarbon are replaced by other atoms or groups of atoms, such as **halogens**. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• A classic example is the **chlorination of methane**. In the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) light** or **diffused sunlight**, a chlorine atom replaces a hydrogen atom in **Methane (CH4)** to form **Chloromethane (CH3Cl)** and **Hydrogen Chloride (HCl)**.
 
• This reaction can continue until all the hydrogen atoms in the alkane are substituted. For methane, the sequence ends with **Tetrachloromethane (CCl4)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Addition Reaction:**

 
 
• This reaction is characteristic of **unsaturated hydrocarbons** like **alkenes** (double bonds) and **alkynes** (triple bonds).
 
• In an addition reaction, molecules like **Hydrogen (H2)** or **Bromine (Br2)** are added across the multiple bonds to turn them into saturated compounds. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect for alkanes.***
 
 
 
• **Neutralisation:**
 
 
• This is a chemical reaction between an **acid** and a **base** to produce **salt** and **water**.
 
• Hydrocarbons are generally **neutral** and do not participate in standard acid-base neutralisation. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Polymerisation:**
 
 
• This involves the combination of many small molecules called **monomers** to form a large molecule called a **polymer**.
 
• While **unsaturated** hydrocarbons like **ethene** undergo polymerisation to form **polyethene**, saturated alkanes do not typically exhibit this as a characteristic reaction. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Combustion:**
 
 
• Alkanes react readily with **Oxygen (O2)** upon heating. **Complete combustion** produces **Carbon dioxide (CO2)**, **Water (H2O)**, and a large amount of **heat and light**, making them excellent **fuels**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paraffins:** Alkanes were traditionally called **paraffins** (from Latin **parum** = little, **affinis** = affinity), highlighting their low chemical reactivity toward common reagents like acids, bases, or oxidising agents at **room temperature**.
 
• **Homologous Series:** Alkanes form a series where each member differs from the next by a **-CH2-** unit and has a mass difference of **14 units**.
 
• **Isomerism:** Alkanes with **four or more** carbon atoms (starting from **Butane**) can show **structural isomerism**, where they have the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms.
 
• **Physical State:** At room temperature, the first four alkanes (**Methane, Ethane, Propane, and Butane**) are **gases**, while those from **C5 to C17** are **liquids**, and higher alkanes are **solids**.

questions.question: Xylem is a complex permanent tissue. Which of the following is correct regarding its composition?

options.text: Tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres
Companion cells, tracheids and xylem fibres
Vessels, xylem collenchyma and xylem fibres
Tracheids, sieve cells and phloem parenchyma

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tracheids, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is defined as a **complex permanent tissue** in plants, primarily responsible for the **conduction of water and dissolved minerals** from the roots to the rest of the plant parts.
 
• It is termed a **complex tissue** because it consists of more than one type of cell that coordinates to perform a common function. The four main components of xylem in **angiosperms** are **Tracheids, Vessels, Xylem Parenchyma, and Xylem Fibres**.
 
• **Tracheids, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibres** are all integral parts of the xylem tissue. While **vessels** are also a key component in **flowering plants**, the provided option correctly identifies three valid xylem constituents. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Companion cells** are a component of **Phloem**, not xylem. They help in the loading and unloading of sugars into sieve tubes. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Collenchyma** is a **simple permanent tissue** that provides mechanical support to young stems and petioles; it is not a sub-type of xylem tissue. Xylem has its own supporting tissue known as **Xylem Fibres** (or sclerenchyma). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sieve cells** and **phloem parenchyma** are specialized cells belonging to the **Phloem**, which is the vascular tissue responsible for transporting **organic nutrients (food)**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Xylem:**

 
 
• **Tracheids:** These are **elongated, tube-like dead cells** with thick, **lignified walls** and tapering ends. They are the primary water-conducting elements in **Gymnosperms** and lower vascular plants.
 
• **Vessels:** Long, cylindrical structures formed by several cells called **vessel members**. They have **perforated end walls** and are much more efficient at water transport than tracheids. They are characteristic features of **Angiosperms**.
 
• **Xylem Parenchyma:** These are the only **living cells** in the xylem tissue. They have thin **cellulosic walls** and function mainly in the **storage of food** (starch or fat) and the **lateral conduction** of water.
 
• **Xylem Fibres:** These are **dead cells** with highly thickened **lignified walls** and obliterated central lumens. Their primary function is to provide **mechanical strength and support** to the plant body.
 
 
 
• **Direction of Flow:** Unlike phloem, which exhibits **bidirectional transport**, the flow in xylem is strictly **unidirectional** (from roots upwards to the leaves).
 
• **Wood:** In botanical terms, the **secondary xylem** produced during the **secondary growth** of a plant is what we commonly refer to as **wood**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolutionary Fact:** In **Gymnosperms** (like pines and cedars), **vessels are absent**; water is conducted almost entirely through **tracheids**.
 
• **Primary Xylem:** It is categorized into **Protoxylem** (first formed) and **Metaxylem** (later formed). In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the center (**Endarch condition**), while in roots, it lies towards the periphery (**Exarch condition**).
 
• **Lignification:** The deposition of **lignin** in the cell walls of tracheids and vessels provides the structural rigidity necessary to withstand the **negative pressure** generated during **transpiration**.

questions.question: What is the process known for removing impurities from ores?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concentration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concentration** of ore, also known as **ore dressing** or **beneficiation**, is the mechanical and physical process used to remove **gangue** (unwanted earthy impurities like **sand**, **clay**, and **rocks**) from the mined ore. It increases the percentage of the **metal** in the ore. ***Hence, the correct answer is Concentration.***
 
• **Refining** refers to the final purification of the **crude metal** obtained after extraction processes like reduction. It is not the primary step for removing impurities from the raw ore but from the extracted metal itself. ***Hence, Statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Roasting** is a chemical metallurgical process where **sulfide ores** are heated strongly in the **presence of excess air** to convert them into **metal oxides**. While it removes some volatile impurities, its primary function is chemical transformation. ***Hence, Statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Smelting** is the process of extracting a metal from its ore by heating it beyond its **melting point**, usually in the presence of **flux** and a **reducing agent** like **carbon** or **coke**. It involves **chemical reduction** rather than just the physical removal of impurities. ***Hence, Statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydraulic Washing (Gravity Separation)**:

 
 
• This method utilizes the difference in **specific gravities** between the ore and the gangue particles.
 
• A stream of **running water** is used to wash the powdered ore; the **lighter gangue** particles are washed away, while the **heavier ore** particles settle down. This is commonly used for **oxide ores** of **Iron** and **Tin**.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Separation**:
 
 
• This technique is applied when either the **ore** or the **impurities** possess **magnetic properties**.
 
• The crushed ore is passed over a **conveyor belt** moving over a **magnetic roller**. Magnetic materials like **Magnetite (Fe3O4)** or **Pyrolusite (MnO2)** are separated from non-magnetic gangue.
 
 
 
• **Froth Flotation Process**:
 
 
• This is a widely used method for concentrating **sulfide ores** such as **Galena (PbS)** and **Copper Pyrites (CuFeS2)**.
 
• It is based on the principle of **preferential wettability**, where ore particles are wetted by **oil** (like **pine oil**) and gangue particles are wetted by **water**. **Collectors** and **froth stabilizers** are added to facilitate the formation of a stable froth that carries the ore to the surface.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Method (Leaching)**:
 
 
• This is used when the ore is soluble in a **specific solvent** while the impurities are not.
 
• In the **Bayer’s process** for **Aluminium**, **Bauxite** is treated with concentrated **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** at **473-523 K**, leaving behind impurities like **Ferric oxide** and **Silica**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gangue**: The unwanted earthly materials associated with ores are called **gangue** or **matrix**.
 
• **Flux**: A substance added during smelting to remove non-fusible impurities by converting them into a fusible **slag**. For example, **CaO** is used as a basic flux to remove acidic **SiO2**.
 
• **Calcination**: Often compared to roasting, **calcination** involves heating the ore in the **absence** or **limited supply of air**, typically used for **carbonates** (like **Zinc Carbonate**) and **hydrated oxides**.
 
• **Electrolytic Refining**: This is a **Refining** technique used for metals like **Copper** and **Zinc**, where **99.9%** purity is achieved by using the impure metal as the **anode** and pure metal as the **cathode** in an **electrolyte**.

questions.question: A force of 50 N acts perpendicular to a surface of area 0.1 { m}² . What are the values of thrust and pressure exerted on the surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thrust = 50.0 N; Pressure = 500.0 Pa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Thrust:** Thrust is the force acting perpendicular to a surface. In this case, a force of **50 N** acts perpendicular to the surface. This means the thrust is **50 N**. Hence, the value of thrust is correct.
 
• **Pressure:** Pressure is defined as force per unit area. The formula is:
 
 
• Pressure = Force ÷ Area
 
• Given force = **50 N**, Area = **0.1 m²**
 
• Pressure = 50 ÷ 0.1 = **500 Pa**
 
 
 
• The provided values for thrust (**50 N**) and pressure (**500 Pa**) are consistent with the given conditions and calculations.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the process of budding in organisms like Hydra?

options.text: A bud forms only during sexual reproduction and fuses with the parent organism.
A bud forms as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division and detaches when mature.
A bud forms from specialised cells inside the organism and remains attached for life.
A bud forms from a broken body part and grows into a new organism.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A bud forms as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division and detaches when mature.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Budding** is an asexual reproduction process observed in organisms like **Hydra**, yeast, and some other species.
 
• In this process, a bud forms as an **outgrowth** on the body of the parent organism due to **repeated mitotic cell division.**
 
• The bud remains attached to the parent organism while it grows and matures, drawing nutrients and support from the parent.
 
• Once the bud is fully developed, it **detaches** from the parent and becomes an independent organism capable of surviving on its own.
 
• This process ensures the **continuity of the species** without the need for gamete fusion, as seen in sexual reproduction. **Hydra** is a well-known example of organisms reproducing through budding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "A bud forms only during sexual reproduction and fuses with the parent organism" – This is **incorrect**. Budding is a form of **asexual reproduction**, and the bud does not fuse with the parent; it detaches to form a new organism.
 
• **Option 3:** "A bud forms from specialized cells inside the organism and remains attached for life" – This is **incorrect**. The bud forms externally and detaches once it matures.
 
• **Option 4:** "A bud forms from a broken body part and grows into a new organism" – This is **incorrect**. This description refers to **regeneration**, not budding. For example, starfish regenerate lost arms, but this is not budding.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Budding:**
 
 
• Budding is common in **Hydra**, **yeast**, and certain plants and fungi.
 
• In **yeast**, the process involves the formation of a small bulge on the parent cell, which grows and eventually separates as a new cell.
 
• In **Hydra**, budding occurs through mitotic cell division in the body wall, forming a miniature version of the parent.
 
• This process is energy-efficient as it does not require the production of gametes or mating.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Asexual Reproduction Methods:**
 
 
• **Fragmentation:** Seen in organisms like **spirogyra**, where the body breaks into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new organism.
 
• **Binary Fission:** Found in bacteria, where the organism divides into two identical daughter cells.
 
• **Sporulation:** Seen in fungi and some plants, where spores develop into new organisms under favorable conditions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Budding:**
 
 
• Ensures **rapid reproduction** in favorable conditions.
 
• Helps maintain the population of species in stable environments.
 
• Simple and efficient mechanism for producing genetically identical offspring.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydra:**

 
 
• Hydra is a **freshwater organism** belonging to the phylum **Cnidaria**.
 
• It reproduces both sexually and asexually, with budding being its common mode of asexual reproduction.
 
• Hydra’s ability to regenerate is another significant characteristic, which allows it to recover lost body parts.
 
 
 
• **Yeast:**
 
 
• Yeast is a unicellular fungus that reproduces primarily through budding.
 
• It is used in baking, brewing, and scientific research due to its rapid growth and easy genetic manipulation.
 
• In yeast, a small bud appears, grows, and eventually separates to form an independent organism.

questions.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the microscopic observation of onion peel cells?

options.text: The size of the onion decides the shape of its individual cells
All onions are made up of similar small structures called cells
Onion bulbs contain different cell types for different functions
Each onion peel contains cells of different composition

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All onions are made up of similar small structures called cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The microscopic observation of **onion peel** (the **epidermis**) demonstrates that all onions, regardless of their **size**, **shape**, or **variety**, are composed of basic structural units known as **cells**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• When an onion peel is examined under a **compound microscope**, it reveals a pattern of **rectangular** or **brick-shaped** compartments arranged in a regular fashion, each containing a **nucleus** and **cytoplasm**.
 
• The **size** of the onion bulb does not affect the **shape** or **size** of these individual cells; a large onion and a small onion will both show identical-looking cellular structures under magnification. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **onion peel** is a **homogenous tissue** layer (the **protective epidermis**), meaning the cells within this specific layer are very similar in **composition** and **function**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• While an entire **onion plant** has different cell types for different functions (such as **root cells** or **vascular cells**), the specific observation of the **peel** primarily highlights the **uniformity** of the **dermal tissue** rather than a diversity of functions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of an Onion Cell:** As a typical **plant cell**, an onion cell contains a **rigid cell wall** made of **cellulose**, which provides **structural support**. It also features a large **central vacuole** that maintains **turgor pressure** and pushes the **nucleus** to the **periphery**.
 
• **The Role of Staining:** Because most cell organelles are **transparent**, stains like **Safranin** or **Iodine solution** are used. These **chemicals** color the **nucleus** and **cell wall** more intensely, making them clearly visible under **light microscopy**.
 
• **Cell Theory:** The observation of onion cells is a fundamental piece of evidence for the **Cell Theory**, formulated by **Matthias Schleiden** and **Theodor Schwann** in **1838-1839**. This theory states that **all living things** are made of **cells** and cells are the **basic unit of life**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The term "cell" was first coined by **Robert Hooke** in **1665** after observing **cork**. Later, in **1831**, **Robert Brown** discovered the **nucleus** within the plant cell, which is easily seen in onion peel preparations.
 
• **Onion Bulb Botany:** The **onion** (***Allium cepa***) is a **modified underground stem** called a **bulb**. The "peels" we observe are the **epidermal layers** of the fleshy **leaves** that store **food** and **nutrients** for the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Experimental Procedure:** To observe these cells, a thin **transparent membrane** is stripped from the **concave side** of an onion fleshy scale. It is placed in a **watch glass** with **water** to prevent **dehydration** or **folding**.
 
• **Mounting:** The specimen is mounted on a **glass slide** with a drop of **glycerin** (to prevent drying) and covered with a **coverslip**. It is vital to avoid **air bubbles** during this process for a clear **microscopic view**.
 
• **Magnification:** Typical classroom observations use a **low-power objective** (**10x**) for a wide field of view and a **high-power objective** (**40x**) to see the **nucleus** and **cell boundaries** in detail.
 
• **Biological Classification:** Onions are **monocotyledons**, and their cells are often used in labs because they are large, easy to extract, and provide a **single-layer** view of **eukaryotic** architecture.

questions.question: What is the key realization that can lead to more sustainable use of natural resources?

options.text: Selfish exploitation causes environmental harm and misery
Only future generations must benefit from resources

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Selfish exploitation causes environmental harm and misery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The core realization for **sustainable resource management** is that **unregulated selfish exploitation** of **natural resources** inevitably leads to **ecological degradation** and human suffering. This is often described in **environmental economics** as the **Tragedy of the Commons**.
 
• When individuals or entities prioritize **short-term profits** over **long-term stability**, they deplete **renewable resources** (like **forests** and **fisheries**) and **non-renewable resources** (like **minerals** and **fossil fuels**) beyond their **carrying capacity**.
 
• This exploitation results in **environmental harm**, such as **biodiversity loss**, **soil erosion**, and **climate change**, which directly causes **socio-economic misery** by destroying livelihoods and reducing the **quality of life** for present and future populations.
 
• Recognizing the **interconnectedness** of **ecosystems** helps society understand that **sustainable use** is not just an **ethical choice** but a **biological necessity** for survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development:** This concept was famously defined in the **Brundtland Report** (also known as **Our Common Future**) in **1987** as development that meets the needs of the **present** without compromising the ability of **future generations** to meet their own needs.
 
• **The Three Pillars:** Sustainability is built on **three interconnected pillars**: **Environmental Protection**, **Social Equity**, and **Economic Viability**. Focusing solely on **unlimited growth** (Option 2) ignores the **biophysical limits** of **Earth**.
 
• **Intergenerational Equity:** This **legal** and **ethical principle** suggests that **natural resources** belong to all generations. questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the need for macronutrients in plants is correct?

options.text: Macronutrients are not required by plants at all.
Macronutrients are required by plants in large quantities.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Macronutrients are required by plants in large quantities.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Macronutrients are required by plants in large quantities** because they are essential for the growth, development, and metabolic processes of plants. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Macronutrients include nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), and sulfur (S)**. These elements play crucial roles in photosynthesis, enzyme activation, cell division, and nutrient transport.
 
• **Macronutrients are not harmful to plants** if absorbed correctly. However, excess or deficiency of macronutrients can lead to plant disorders. *Hence, the statement "Macronutrients are harmful to plants if absorbed" is incorrect.*
 
• **Macronutrients are needed throughout the plant's life cycle**, not just during flowering. They are vital for vegetative growth, reproduction, and overall physiological functions. *Hence, the statement "Macronutrients are needed only during flowering" is incorrect.*
 
• **Macronutrients are indispensable for plant health**. They cannot be substituted or ignored, as they are required for the proper functioning of various physiological and biochemical pathways. *Hence, the statement "Macronutrients are not required by plants at all" is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of Macronutrients:**

 
 
• **Nitrogen (N):** Promotes vegetative growth, chlorophyll formation, and protein synthesis.
 
• **Phosphorus (P):** Essential for energy transfer (ATP) and root development.
 
• **Potassium (K):** Regulates water uptake, enzyme activation, and disease resistance.
 
• **Calcium (Ca):** Strengthens cell walls and aids cell division.
 
• **Magnesium (Mg):** Central component of chlorophyll and assists in enzyme activation.
 
• **Sulfur (S):** Required for amino acids and protein synthesis.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Macronutrient Deficiency:**
 
 
• **Nitrogen deficiency:** Yellowing of leaves (chlorosis) and stunted growth.
 
• **Phosphorus deficiency:** Purple discoloration of leaves and poor root development.
 
• **Potassium deficiency:** Leaf curling and browning edges.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Macronutrients:**
 
 
• **Natural sources:** Organic matter, manure, and compost.
 
• **Synthetic fertilizers:** Urea, DAP (Di-ammonium phosphate), and Muriate of Potash.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Proper macronutrient management increases crop yield and quality.
 
• A balanced supply prevents nutrient-related diseases and ensures sustainable farming.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Agricultural Practices:**

 
 
• **Integrated Nutrient Management (INM):** Combines organic and inorganic fertilizers for balanced nutrient supply.
 
• **Precision Farming:** Uses technology to optimize macronutrient application based on soil and crop requirements.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impacts:**
 
 
• Excessive macronutrient use can lead to soil degradation and water pollution.
 
• Proper nutrient management reduces greenhouse gas emissions and promotes sustainable agriculture.

questions.question: What is the purpose of anodising aluminium metals?

options.text: To make it more reactive with air
To form a protective oxide layer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To form a protective oxide layer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anodising** is a sophisticated **electrolytic process** used to increase the thickness of the natural **oxide layer** on the surface of metal parts, most commonly **aluminium**.
 
• During this process, a clean **aluminium** article is made the **anode** in an electrolytic bath, usually containing an acid such as **dilute sulphuric acid**.
 
• When an electric current is passed through the electrolyte, **oxygen gas** is evolved at the **anode**, which reacts with the **aluminium** to form a thick, uniform, and **protective layer of aluminium oxide (Al2O3)**.
 
• The primary objective of this process is to provide **corrosion resistance** and enhance the **durability** of the metal by creating a barrier against environmental factors. ***Hence, the correct answer is to form a protective oxide layer.***
 
• Unlike paint or plating, this **oxide layer** is fully integrated with the underlying **aluminium** substrate, so it cannot chip or peel off.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aesthetic and Decorative Uses**:

 
 
• The **anodic oxide layer** has a **porous structure** immediately after the process. These pores can be used to absorb **dyes** or **pigments**.
 
• This allows **aluminium** products to be finished in a wide variety of **colors** while retaining the metallic texture, which is common in **consumer electronics** and **cookware**.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Properties**:
 
 
• While **aluminium** is an excellent conductor of electricity, **aluminium oxide** is an **insulator**.
 
• Therefore, **anodising** actually **decreases** the surface **electrical conductivity**, which can be useful in specific engineering applications where insulation is required.
 
 
 
• **Surface Hardness**:
 
 
• The **anodised layer** is significantly harder than the base metal. This provides excellent **abrasion resistance** and **wear resistance**, extending the lifespan of components used in **machinery** and **transportation**.
 
 
 
• **Adhesion**:
 
 
• The process provides a much better **adhesion** surface for **paints**, **primers**, and **glues** compared to bare metal, making it a critical pre-treatment step in many manufacturing workflows.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Common Applications**: **Anodised aluminium** is extensively used in **aerospace** for aircraft skins, **architecture** for window frames and roofs, and in **automotive** parts for its lightweight and rust-proof nature.
 
• **Maintenance**: Because the **oxide layer** is chemically stable, **anodised** surfaces require very low maintenance and are resistant to **UV radiation**, meaning the color does not fade easily over **years** of exposure.
 
• **Environmental Safety**: **Anodising** is considered an **environmentally safe** metal finishing process as it does not involve **heavy metals** like lead or cadmium, and the chemical by-products are often neutralized before disposal.
 
• **Comparison**: While **aluminium** forms a natural **oxide film** when exposed to **air**, this natural layer is very thin (approx **2-3 nanometers**). **Industrial anodising** can increase this thickness to **5 to 25 micrometers** or more, depending on the application.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Using the mirror formula, what will be the image distance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-60 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mirror formula** provides a quantitative relationship between the **object distance (u)**, the **image distance (v)**, and the **focal length (f)** of a spherical mirror. The formula is expressed as **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the **focal length (f)** is always considered **negative** according to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**. In this problem, the given focal length is **20 cm**, so we use **f = -20 cm**.
 
• The **object distance (u)** is the distance from the **pole** of the mirror to the object. Since the object is placed in front of the mirror, the distance is measured against the direction of incident light, making it **negative**. Here, **u = -30 cm**.
 
• To find the **image distance (v)**, we rearrange the mirror formula: **1/v = 1/f - 1/u**. Substituting the values: **1/v = 1/(-20) - 1/(-30)**.
 
• This simplifies to **1/v = -1/20 + 1/30**. By taking the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of **20 and 30**, which is **60**, the equation becomes **1/v = (-3 + 2) / 60**.
 
• Solving further, **1/v = -1/60**, which gives the result **v = -60 cm**. ***Hence, the image distance is -60 cm and the correct option is -60 cm.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of the Image:** Since the **image distance (v)** is **negative**, the image is formed in front of the mirror. This indicates that the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** Magnification is defined as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, also given by **m = -v/u**. In this case, **m = -(-60) / (-30)**, which equals **-2**. A magnification of **-2** means the image is **magnified** (twice the size of the object) and **inverted**.
 
• **Position relative to Center of Curvature:** The **Radius of Curvature (R)** of this mirror is **R = 2f = 40 cm**. Since the object is placed at **30 cm** (between the **Focus at 20 cm** and the **Center of Curvature at 40 cm**), the image must form **beyond the Center of Curvature** (greater than **40 cm**). Our result of **60 cm** aligns with this optical principle.
 
• **Concave Mirror Characteristics:** Often called a **converging mirror**, it has the ability to produce **real** as well as **virtual** images depending on the object's position relative to the **focal point**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention Rules:** Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are taken as **positive**, while those measured in the opposite direction are **negative**. All distances are measured from the **pole (P)** of the mirror.
 
• **Focal Lengths:** It is a **fact** that the **focal length** of a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, whereas the focal length of a **convex mirror** is always **positive**.
 
• **Real vs Virtual:** A **positive image distance (v)** for a mirror would imply a **virtual image** formed behind the mirror, while a **negative image distance** signifies a **real image**.
 
• **Practical Uses:** Concave mirrors are utilized in **torches**, **search-lights**, and **vehicle headlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light, as well as by **dentists** to see larger images of teeth.

questions.question: The discovery of which subatomic particle led to the development of Thomson's model?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The discovery of the **electron** by **Sir J.J. Thomson** in **1897** was the primary catalyst for the development of the first modern atomic model.
 
• Thomson conducted experiments using a **Cathode Ray Tube (CRT)**, where he observed that rays were deflected away from a negatively charged plate and toward a positively charged plate, indicating they consisted of **negatively charged particles**.
 
• Following this discovery, **Thomson** proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** (also known as the **Watermelon Model**) in **1904** to explain the structure of the atom.
 
• In this model, the atom was envisioned as a **positively charged sphere** in which **negatively charged electrons** were embedded, similar to seeds in a watermelon or raisins in a pudding.
 
• This discovery was revolutionary because it proved that the atom was not an indivisible particle, as **John Dalton** had previously proposed in his **Atomic Theory**, but instead contained smaller **subatomic particles**.
 
• The model also established the concept of **electrical neutrality**, suggesting that the total positive charge of the sphere was exactly balanced by the total negative charge of the embedded electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Proton**:

 
 
• While **Eugen Goldstein** observed **canal rays** (positive ions) in **1886**, the **proton** was identified as a fundamental subatomic particle by **Ernest Rutherford**.
 
• In **1919**, **Rutherford** proved that the nucleus of a hydrogen atom was present in other nuclei, leading to the naming of the **proton** in **1920**.
 
• The **proton** carries a **positive charge** of **+1.602 x 10^-19 Coulombs** and has a mass approximately **1836 times** that of an electron.
 
 
 
• **Neutron**:
 
 
• The **neutron** was discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**.
 
• He bombarded **Beryllium** with **alpha particles** and observed a new type of radiation that consisted of uncharged particles with a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.
 
• The discovery of the **neutron** explained why the atomic mass was often more than double the atomic number and helped in the understanding of **isotopes**.
 
 
 
• **Positron**:
 
 
• The **positron** is the **antiparticle** of the electron, discovered by **Carl D. Anderson** in **1932** while studying **cosmic rays**.
 
• It has the **same mass** as an electron but carries a **positive charge**. It was the first evidence of **antimatter**.
 
 
 
• **Rutherford’s Atomic Model**:
 
 
• Developed in **1911** following the **Alpha-particle Scattering Experiment** (Gold Foil Experiment).
 
• This model superseded Thomson's model by proposing that the atom has a tiny, dense, **positively charged nucleus** at its center, with electrons revolving around it, much like planets around the sun.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chronology of Discovery**: The **electron** (1897) was discovered first, followed by the **proton** (identified in 1919), and finally the **neutron** (1932).
 
• **Charge-to-Mass Ratio**: J.J. Thomson is also famous for measuring the **charge-to-mass ratio (e/m)** of the electron, which he found to be constant regardless of the gas used in the discharge tube.
 
• **Nobel Prize**: **J.J. Thomson** was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1906** for his work on the conduction of electricity by gases and the discovery of the electron.

questions.question: The reaction between CaO and H₂O is highly exothermic and produces Ca(OH)₂. This is an example of:
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Combination reaction**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between **Calcium Oxide (CaO)** and **Water (H2O)** is a classic example of a **Combination reaction**. In this process, **Quicklime (CaO)** reacts vigorously with water to produce **Slaked Lime [Ca(OH)2]**.
 
• A **Combination reaction** is defined as a chemical reaction where **two or more reactants** combine to form a **single product**. In this specific case, the two reactants (CaO and H2O) merge to form one product [Ca(OH)2]. *Hence, the statement regarding it being a combination reaction is correct.*
 
• This reaction is characterized by being **highly exothermic**. An **Exothermic reaction** is one in which **heat energy** is released into the surroundings. During the formation of **Slaked Lime**, a significant amount of **thermal energy** is evolved, which can even cause the water to boil. 
 
• The chemical equation for this process is: **CaO (s) + H2O (l) → Ca(OH)2 (aq) + Heat**. This demonstrates the synthesis of a new substance from simpler ones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Chemical Reactions:**

 
 
• **Displacement Reaction:** This occurs when a **more reactive element** displaces a **less reactive element** from its compound. An example is the reaction between **Iron (Fe)** and **Copper Sulphate (CuSO4)**, where iron replaces copper.
 
• **Double Displacement Reaction:** These are reactions in which there is an **exchange of ions** between the reactants to form new compounds. Often, one of the products formed is an **insoluble precipitate** (e.g., the reaction between **Barium Chloride** and **Sodium Sulphate**).
 
• **Rearrangement Reaction:** This involves the **structural reorganization** of a molecule to form an **isomer**. The atoms remain the same, but their connectivity or spatial arrangement changes.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• The **Slaked Lime** produced is extensively used for **whitewashing** walls. After application, it reacts slowly with **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** in the air to form a thin layer of **Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3)**.
 
• This **Calcium Carbonate** layer gives a **shiny, white finish** to the walls, usually appearing **2 to 3 days** after the whitewashing process.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Nomenclature:**

 
 
• **CaO** is chemically known as **Calcium Oxide** and is commercially referred to as **Quicklime** or **Burnt Lime**.
 
• **Ca(OH)2** is chemically known as **Calcium Hydroxide** and is commonly called **Slaked Lime**. When dissolved in water, the clear solution is known as **Lime Water**.
 
 
 
• **Thermodynamic Context:**
 
 
• The **highly exothermic** nature of the reaction is a critical safety consideration in **industrial and laboratory** settings, as the **intensity of heat** released can be dangerous if not controlled.
 
• In contrast to **Exothermic reactions**, **Endothermic reactions** are those that **absorb heat** from the surroundings to proceed, such as the **decomposition** of **Calcium Carbonate** back into **CaO** and **CO2**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT present in animal cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** are **absent in animal cells**. These organelles are specific to plant cells and some algae, where they are responsible for **photosynthesis**, a process that converts light energy into chemical energy stored as glucose.
 
• Animal cells do not perform photosynthesis as they obtain energy by consuming organic matter rather than producing it. *Hence, chloroplasts are absent in animal cells.*
 
• **Nucleus**, **plasma membrane**, and **cytoplasm** are present in both animal and plant cells. These are essential components for cellular function. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• The **nucleus** houses the genetic material (DNA) and controls cellular activities, making it an indispensable organelle in all eukaryotic cells.
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also known as the cell membrane, surrounds the cell, providing structural support, protection, and regulating the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the jelly-like substance filling the cell, where various metabolic processes and organelle activities take place. It is present in all cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chloroplast:**

 
 
• Chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles found in plant cells and certain protists like algae.
 
• They contain the pigment **chlorophyll**, which captures light energy for photosynthesis.
 
• Chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes, enabling them to produce some of their own proteins.
 
• They are responsible for converting light energy into glucose and oxygen, which are essential for the survival of plants and indirectly for all living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:**
 
 
• The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle present in all eukaryotic cells.
 
• It contains the cell's genetic material in the form of DNA, organized into chromosomes.
 
• It regulates essential cellular functions such as growth, metabolism, protein synthesis, and cell division.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• The plasma membrane is a semi-permeable structure made of a phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins.
 
• It regulates the movement of molecules such as nutrients, waste, and ions in and out of the cell.
 
• In animal cells, it is the outermost layer, whereas in plant cells, it is located beneath the cell wall.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm:**
 
 
• The cytoplasm is the gel-like substance enclosed within the cell membrane.
 
• It contains organelles such as mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and Golgi apparatus, as well as cytosol, a fluid component.
 
• It is the site of various cellular processes, including glycolysis and intracellular transport.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plant vs. Animal Cells:**

 
 
• Plant cells have a rigid cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells.
 
• Animal cells have centrioles and lysosomes, which are not typically found in plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• This process occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, where light energy is converted into chemical energy.
 
• The equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
 
 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory:**
 
 
• Chloroplasts and mitochondria are believed to have originated from free-living prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.
 
• This theory is supported by the presence of their own DNA and double membranes.

questions.question: Which of the following plants reproduces by means of spores?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moss**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mosses** belong to the **Bryophyta** division of the plant kingdom. They are **non-vascular plants** that do not produce **flowers**, **fruits**, or **seeds**.
 
• These plants reproduce primarily through **spores**, which are **unicellular** reproductive units. These spores are produced in a structure called a **capsule** or **sporangium**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Unlike higher plants, mosses do not have true **roots**, **stems**, or **leaves**. Instead, they have **rhizoids** that help in anchoring the plant to the **substrate** and absorbing **moisture**.
 
• The plants **Rose**, **Egg plant** (Brinjal), and **Gram** are all **Angiosperms**. Angiosperms are **flowering plants** that reproduce through **seeds** enclosed within a **fruit**. ***Hence, statements 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect.***
 
• **Mosses** exhibit a life cycle known as **alternation of generations**, where the **gametophyte** (the green leafy part) is the **dominant phase**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Plants based on Reproduction:**

 
 
• **Cryptogams:** These are **non-flowering** and **seedless** plants. They reproduce via **spores**. Examples include **Algae** (Thallophyta), **Mosses** (Bryophyta), and **Ferns** (Pteridophyta).
 
• **Phanerogams:** These are **seed-bearing** plants. They are further divided into **Gymnosperms** (naked seeds) and **Angiosperms** (seeds inside fruits).
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Mosses:**
 
 
• They usually grow in **damp**, **humid**, and **shady** locations to facilitate **fertilization**, as they require a film of **water** for the **sperm** to swim to the **egg**.
 
• **Sphagnum**, a type of moss, is often used as **fuel** (peat) and in **horticulture** due to its high **water-retention capacity**.
 
 
 
• **Seeds vs. Spores:**
 
 
• A **seed** is a **multicellular** structure containing an **embryo** and a **food supply** (endosperm) protected by a **seed coat**.
 
• A **spore** is typically **unicellular**, **microscopic**, and lacks the **nutrient reserves** found in seeds, making them more vulnerable to **environmental stress**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amphibians of the Plant Kingdom:** **Bryophytes** (like mosses) are frequently referred to by this name because, while they live on **soil**, they are absolutely dependent on **external water** for **sexual reproduction**.
 
• **Vascular Tissue:** Unlike **Rose** or **Gram**, mosses lack **Xylem** and **Phloem** (specialized tissues for conducting water and minerals). This limits their **size**, which is why they remain **small** and **low-growing**.
 
• **Ecological Importance:** Mosses are among the **first organisms** to colonize **bare rocks** along with **lichens**. They decompose **rocks** and form **soil**, making the environment suitable for the **growth of higher plants**.
 
• **Examples of Spore-bearing Plants:** Other than mosses, **Ferns** (Pteridophytes), **Horsetails**, and **Liverworts** also reproduce through **spores**.

questions.question: A distance–time graph is a curve rather than a straight line. What does this indicate?

options.text: The body is moving with uniform acceleration.
The body is moving with non-uniform speed.
The body is moving with uniform speed.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The body is moving with non-uniform speed.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **distance–time graph** represents the motion of a body by plotting distance on the y-axis and time on the x-axis.
 
• If the graph is a **curve**, it indicates that the body is moving with **non-uniform speed**. This implies that the distance covered by the body changes irregularly over equal intervals of time.
 
• A straight-line distance–time graph would signify **uniform speed**, where the body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. However, a curve represents variability in speed.
 
• **Non-uniform motion** occurs when the object accelerates or decelerates, leading to changes in speed at different points during its motion.
 
• **Acceleration** is not necessarily uniform in this case, as the changing slope of the curve signifies irregular changes in speed over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Uniform Motion:**

 
 
• An object is said to be in uniform motion if it covers **equal distances in equal intervals of time**. This is represented by a straight-line distance–time graph.
 
• Example: A car moving at a constant speed of 60 km/h on a highway.
 
 
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:**
 
 
• In non-uniform motion, the object covers **unequal distances in equal intervals of time**. This is represented by a curved distance–time graph.
 
• Example: A cyclist slowing down or speeding up while riding.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• Acceleration is the **rate of change of velocity** of a body. It can be uniform or non-uniform.
 
• If the slope of the distance–time graph changes steadily, the body might be undergoing uniform acceleration. If the slope changes irregularly, it indicates non-uniform acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of a Distance–Time Graph:**
 
 
• **Horizontal line:** The body is stationary.
 
• **Straight inclined line:** Uniform speed.
 
• **Curved line:** Non-uniform speed or accelerated motion.
 
• **Steeper curve:** Higher speed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Differences Between Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion:**

 
 
• **Uniform Motion:** Constant speed, straight-line graph, no acceleration.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:** Varying speed, curved graph, acceleration present.
 
 
 
• **Real-Life Examples:**
 
 
• **Uniform Motion:** A clock's second hand moving at a constant rate.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:** A car navigating through city traffic.
 
 
 
• **Graph Interpretation:**
 
 
• The **slope** of a distance–time graph determines speed.
 
• A **steeper slope** indicates higher speed, while a flatter slope shows slower motion.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)** are infections primarily passed from one person to another through vaginal, anal, or oral sexual contact, caused by more than **30 different pathogens** including **bacteria**, **viruses**, and **parasites**.
 
• **Condoms** are highly effective **barrier methods** that prevent the transmission of infections by blocking the direct exchange of **bodily fluids** like **semen**, **pre-ejaculate**, and **vaginal secretions**.
 
• According to scientific data, consistent and correct use of **latex condoms** reduces the risk of **Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)** transmission by approximately **80% to 90%**.
 
• Condoms also significantly lower the transmission rates of other fluid-borne bacterial infections such as **Gonorrhea** (caused by *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*) and **Chlamydia** (caused by *Chlamydia trachomatis*) by preventing the pathogens from reaching the **mucous membranes**.
 
• While they are most effective against fluid-borne diseases, they also provide a degree of protection against infections spread through **skin-to-skin contact**, such as **Syphilis** and **Genital Herpes**, provided the infected area is covered by the barrier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pathogen Categories**:

 
 
• **Bacterial STIs**: Infections like **Syphilis**, **Gonorrhea**, and **Chlamydia** can be cured with a full course of **antibiotics** prescribed by medical professionals.
 
• **Viral STIs**: Infections like **HIV**, **Human Papillomavirus (HPV)**, and **Hepatitis B** are generally incurable but manageable with **antiviral therapy** and **vaccines**.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Misconceptions**:
 
 
• **Antibiotic Prophylaxis**: Taking **antibiotics** before sexual activity without a medical diagnosis is ineffective against **viruses** and contributes to the global threat of **antimicrobial resistance**.
 
• **Environmental Factors**: The **time of day** or the **setting** of sexual activity has zero biological impact on the **viability** or **transmission** of STI-causing pathogens.

questions.question: What gas is typically released when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **Ethanoic acid** (commonly known as **Acetic acid**) reacts with **Sodium carbonate** (also known as **Washing soda**), a chemical reaction occurs that releases **Carbon dioxide gas**.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is **2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2**. In this process, **Ethanoic acid** reacts with the metal carbonate to produce **Sodium ethanoate** (a salt), **Water**, and **Carbon dioxide**.
 
• The evolution of **Carbon dioxide gas** is observed as **brisk effervescence**, which refers to the rapid formation of bubbles in the liquid as the gas escapes.
 
• This reaction is a characteristic property of **carboxylic acids**, where they react with **carbonates** and **bicarbonates** to evolve **CO2**, serving as a common laboratory test to identify the presence of a **carboxyl group**.
 
• The gas evolved can be identified by passing it through **lime water** (calcium hydroxide), which will turn **milky** due to the formation of **Calcium carbonate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ethanoic Acid (CH3COOH):**

 
 
• It is a **weak organic acid** and the second simplest **carboxylic acid** after formic acid.
 
• In its concentrated form, it is called **Glacial Acetic Acid** because it freezes at **16.6 degrees Celsius**, forming ice-like crystals.
 
• It is widely used in the food industry as **Vinegar**, which typically contains **5% to 8%** ethanoic acid by volume.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3):**
 
 
• Commonly known as **Washing Soda**, it is a **basic salt** derived from a strong base and a weak acid.
 
• It is used in **glass manufacturing**, **water softening**, and as a **laboratory reagent**.
 
• When it reacts with acids, it consistently produces **Carbon dioxide**, making it useful in **fire extinguishers** and **effervescent salts**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H2):**
 
 
• Unlike carbonates, when **metals** like **Zinc** or **Magnesium** react with acids, they typically release **Hydrogen gas**.
 
• **Hydrogen** is a colorless, odorless gas that burns with a **pop sound** when a burning splinter is brought near it.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen Gas (O2):**
 
 
• **Oxygen** is not typically released in simple acid-base neutralization or acid-carbonate reactions.
 
• It is usually produced during the **decomposition** of certain oxides or **electrolysis of water**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction with Sodium Bicarbonate:** **Ethanoic acid** also reacts with **Sodium bicarbonate** (**NaHCO3**, or baking soda) to produce the same gas, **Carbon dioxide**. The equation is **CH3COOH + NaHCO3 → CH3COONa + H2O + CO2**.
 
• **Test for Carbon Dioxide:** To confirm the identity of the gas, it is passed through **Lime Water** [**Ca(OH)2**]. The lime water turns **milky** because of the formation of insoluble **Calcium Carbonate** (**CaCO3**). If the gas is passed in excess, the milkiness disappears due to the formation of soluble **Calcium Hydrogen Carbonate** [**Ca(HCO3)2**].
 
• **Functional Group Identification:** The reaction with **Sodium Carbonate** is a standard **analytical test** to distinguish **carboxylic acids** from **phenols** and **alcohols**, as the latter do not typically release **CO2** with carbonates.
 
• **Salt Formation:** The salt formed in this specific reaction, **Sodium ethanoate** (**CH3COONa**), is used in the **textile industry** and as a **buffering agent** in various chemical applications.

questions.question: The speeds of a car, train and bus are in the ratio 6 ∶ 9 ∶ 6. The average speed of the car, bus and train is 77 km/hr. Find the average speed of the car and the train.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds of **Car : Train : Bus** = 6 : 9 : 6

Total ratio parts for average calculation = (6 + 9 + 6) ÷ 3 = 7 units

7 units corresponds to 77 km/hr ⇒ 1 unit = 11 km/hr

Ratio average of **Car and Train** = (6 + 9) ÷ 2 = 7.5 units

Value = 7.5 × 11 = 82.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 82.5 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e895279ffd92f7b5f2e476aba9932cf8e3f3572d6a3ddd628c6b75fa299913a1.png] 

**Given:** Ratio of speeds = 6 : 9 : 6, Average speed of three = 77 km/hr

**Formula:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

⇒ Let the speeds be 6x, 9x, and 6x.

⇒ (6x + 9x + 6x) ÷ 3 = 77

⇒ 21x ÷ 3 = 77

⇒ 7x = 77 ⇒ x = 11

⇒ Average of Car and Train = (6x + 9x) ÷ 2

⇒ 15x ÷ 2 = 7.5x

⇒ 7.5 × 11 = 82.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 82.5 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When combining groups, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Ratio Application

If values are in ratio a:b:c, the average is (a+b+c)/3 multiplied by the constant factor k.

Average Speed for Equal Distance

For two speeds u and v covering equal distances, Average Speed = 2uv ÷ (u + v).</p

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 14 km/h. It goes 28 km downstream in 1 h 45 min. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Time** to hours: 1 h 45 min = 1.75 hours.

**Downstream Speed** = Distance ÷ Time = 28 ÷ 1.75 = 16 km/h.

**Stream Speed** = Downstream Speed − Boat Speed in Still Water.

**Stream Speed** = 16 − 14 = 2 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **boat** in still water (u) = 14 km/h

**Distance** (D) = 28 km

**Time** (t) = 1 h 45 min

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0417c4c3b2af0be48e6cbb767d92f8751bfe1afd9e53796013402a913b825f29.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed (vd) = Speed in still water (u) + Speed of stream (v)

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time (t) = 1 h + 45/60 h = 1 + 3/4 = 7/4 hours = 1.75 hours

⇒ **Downstream Speed** (vd) = 28 ÷ (7/4) = 28 × 4 ÷ 7

⇒ vd = 4 × 4 = 16 km/h

⇒ u + v = 16

⇒ 14 + v = 16

⇒ v = 16 − 14 = 2 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Upstream Speed

It is the net speed of the boat against the stream: Upstream Speed (vᵤ) = u − v.

Speed in Still Water

If downstream and upstream speeds are known, u = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If downstream and upstream speeds are known, v = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.</p

questions.question: A hostel had food provision for 300 students for a month. After 20 days, 50 students left the hostel. How long would the remaining food last? (1 month = 30 days)

Remaining food for **300 students** is for **10 days** (30 − 20 = 10).

Students remaining = 300 − 50 = **250 students**.

Using **M₁D₁ = M₂D₂**: 300 × 10 = 250 × D.

Chain Rule (Work and Person)

Inverse Proportion

questions.question: If the roots of the equation x² - bx + c = 5 differ by 5, then which one of the following is correct ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0, the **difference of roots** is given by |α − β| = √D / |a|.

Rewrite the equation: x² − bx + (c − 5) = 0, where a = 1, b = −b, and constant term = (c − 5).

Difference = 5 ⇒ 5 = √((−b)² − 4 × 1 × (c − 5)) / 1

Squaring both sides: 25 = b² − 4c + 20 ⇒ b² = 4c + 5.

**∴ The correct answer is b² = 4c + 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation: x² − bx + c = 5

Difference of roots (|α − β|) = 5

**Formula Used:**

1. Sum of roots (α + β) = − (coefficient of x) / (coefficient of x²)

2. Product of roots (αβ) = (constant term) / (coefficient of x²)

3. (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ

**Calculations:**

The standard form of the equation is x² − bx + (c − 5) = 0.

⇒ Sum of roots (α + β) = −(−b) / 1 = b

⇒ Product of roots (αβ) = (c − 5) / 1 = c − 5

⇒ Given |α − β| = 5

⇒ (α − β)² = 5² = 25

Substituting sum and product values:

⇒ b² − 4(c − 5) = 25

⇒ b² − 4c + 20 = 25

⇒ b² − 4c = 25 − 20

⇒ b² − 4c = 5

⇒ b² = 4c + 5

**∴ The correct answer is b² = 4c + 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discriminant and Difference of Roots

The **discriminant** (D) is b² − 4ac. The difference of roots is directly related to D by the formula |α − β| = √D / |a|.

Nature of Roots

If D > 0, roots are **real and distinct**. If D = 0, roots are **real and equal**. If D < 0, roots are **imaginary/complex conjugates**.

Vieta's Formulas

For any polynomial equation, the relations between **coefficients** and **roots** are established by Vieta's formulas (Sum = −b/a, Product = c/a).</p

questions.question: If the diameter and the height of a cylinder are 12 cm and 10.5 cm, respectively, then using pi=(22)/(7), find the volume of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check for divisibility by **11** (since π = 22/7 involves a multiple of 11).

Volume = πr²h = (22/7) × 6 × 6 × 10.5

Volume = 11 × 2 × 6 × 6 × 1.5 = 11 × 108 = 1188 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1188 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diameter** (d) = 12 cm ⇒ **Radius** (r) = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm

**Height** (h) = 10.5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a **Cylinder** = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e76157214db662e9e242fe2f205d35aa324c77f28b4c0fbcc3791bdad79792e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (22 ÷ 7) × 6 × 6 × 10.5

⇒ Volume = (22 ÷ 7) × 36 × (21 ÷ 2)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 36 × (3 ÷ 2)

⇒ Volume = 11 × 36 × 3

⇒ Volume = 11 × 108

⇒ Volume = 1188 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1188 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the side surface of a cylinder is given by 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of CSA and the area of two circular bases: 2πr(h + r).

Hollow Cylinder Volume

If R is outer radius and r is inner radius, Volume = π(R² − r²)h.</p

questions.question: By which least number should 196 be multiplied to make it a perfect cube ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Prime factorization** of 196 = 14 × 14 = 2² × 7².

For a **perfect cube**, every prime factor power must be a multiple of 3.

Required factors = 2⁽³−²⁾ × 7⁽³−²⁾ = 2¹ × 7¹ = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6c585d373cb5098f34d1183febeff57a8ab1cf48a64c631eeeffb5eba8098e9.png] 

**Given:** Number = 196

**Method:** Prime Factorization

⇒ 196 = 2 × 98

⇒ 196 = 2 × 2 × 49

⇒ 196 = 2 × 2 × 7 × 7

⇒ To make it a **perfect cube**, we need triplets of each prime factor.

⇒ We have two 2s, so we need one more 2 (2 × 2 × **2**).

⇒ We have two 7s, so we need one more 7 (7 × 7 × **7**).

⇒ **Least number** to be multiplied = 2 × 7 = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Cube Definition

A **perfect cube** is an integer that can be expressed as the cube of another integer (n³). In its prime factorization, all exponents must be **divisible by 3**.

Perfect Square Property

For a number to be a **perfect square**, all exponents in its prime factorization must be **even** (divisible by 2). For example, 196 = 2² × 7² is a perfect square of 14.

Smallest Multiplier for nth Power

To make a number a **perfect kth power**, multiply by factors such that each prime's exponent p becomes the smallest multiple of k ≥ p.</p

questions.question: Find the least value of p so that 246p48 is divisible by 8.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility by 8 rule: Check if the last three digits are divisible by 8.

In 246p48, last three digits are p48. Test least digit p = 0 ⇒ 048 ÷ 8 = 6.

**∴ The correct option is D.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: The number 246p48 is divisible by 8.

Formula Used: A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is divisible by 8.

⇒ The last three digits of 246p48 are p48.

⇒ For the number to be divisible by 8, (100 × p + 48) ÷ 8 must be an integer.

⇒ Testing for the least value of p from the options (p = 0, 1, 2, 4):

⇒ If p = 0: 048 ÷ 8 = 6 (Integer, so p = 0 is a possible value).

⇒ If p = 1: 148 ÷ 8 = 18.5 (Not an integer).

⇒ If p = 2: 248 ÷ 8 = 31 (Integer).

⇒ Comparing the valid values p = 0 and p = 2, the least value is 0.

**∴ The correct option is D.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 2ⁿ

A number is divisible by 2ⁿ if its last n digits are divisible by 2ⁿ. For 2 (2¹), check last digit; for 4 (2²), check last 2 digits; for 8 (2³), check last 3 digits.

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is either 0 or a multiple of 11.</p

questions.question: Arun sold two article for Rs. 631.80 each. On one he gained 17% and on the other he lost 19%. His loss percentage (correct to one decimal place) in the entire transaction is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net loss % when **Selling Price (SP)** is same: **[100(x + y) + 2xy] ÷ [200 + x + y]** where x and y are gain/loss with signs.

Here x = +17 and y = −19. Sum (x+y) = −2, Product (xy) = −323.

Net % = [100(−2) + 2(−323)] ÷ [200 + 17 − 19] = [−200 − 646] ÷ 198 = −846 ÷ 198.

Net loss % = 4.2727...% ≈ 4.3%.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.3%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given → **SP₁ = SP₂ = Rs. 631.80**. Gain₁ = 17%, Loss₂ = 19%.
Formulas: CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 ± Gain/Loss%) | Loss% = (Total CP − Total SP) ÷ Total CP × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5748cf04d1cbfcc99c1875fcc5a51390705a49d46b76ace507b7bd6c45bc107.png] 
⇒ **CP₁** = 631.80 × 100 ÷ 117 = **Rs. 540**.
⇒ **CP₂** = 631.80 × 100 ÷ 81 = **Rs. 780**.
⇒ **Total CP** = 540 + 780 = **Rs. 1320**.
⇒ **Total SP** = 631.80 × 2 = **Rs. 1263.60**.
⇒ **Total Loss** = 1320 − 1263.60 = **Rs. 56.40**.
⇒ **Loss %** = (56.40 ÷ 1320) × 100 = 4.272...% ≈ **4.3%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.3%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Same Selling Price - Equal Gain and Loss

If two articles are sold at the same price, one at a gain of x% and another at a loss of x%, there is always a net loss = (x ÷ 10)² %.

Calculation Accuracy

When values are not equal, use the total CP and total SP method or the combined percentage formula for precision.</p

questions.question: If 3x – 2y = 10 and xy = 11, the value of 27x³ - 8y³ is __________
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the identity: **a³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b)**

Here, a = 3x and b = 2y, so (a − b) = 10 and 3ab = 3(3x)(2y) = 18xy.

Substitute values: 10³ + 18(11)(10) = 1000 + 1980 = 2980.

**∴ The correct answer is 2980.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3x − 2y = 10 and xy = 11

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/426185eadd164bc16f551c60dec644e8c2497e9fe50c639ba1be0aa42ae437f1.png] 

Using the **algebraic identity** for cubes:

(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)

Let a = 3x and b = 2y.

⇒ (3x − 2y)³ = (3x)³ − (2y)³ − 3(3x)(2y)(3x − 2y)

⇒ (3x − 2y)³ = 27x³ − 8y³ − 18xy(3x − 2y)

Substitute the **given values** into the equation:

⇒ (10)³ = 27x³ − 8y³ − 18 × 11 × 10

⇒ 1000 = 27x³ − 8y³ − 1980

⇒ 27x³ − 8y³ = 1000 + 1980

⇒ 27x³ − 8y³ = 2980

**∴ The correct answer is 2980.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube of a Sum

The identity for the cube of a sum is (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b).

Difference of Two Cubes

The expression a³ − b³ can also be factored as (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Sum of Two Cubes

The expression a³ + b³ can be factored as (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).</p
